clue.text: Try eating the whole vegetable

indicators.note: one piece eating another takes it inside itself, so the attempt word swallows the totality word

parts.note: a try is a shot, an attempt
the whole of something is all of it

explanation.surface: An invitation to have a go at eating an entire vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallot is a small onion-like bulb, a kind of vegetable.

clue.text: Combination of drama and musical work, not a failure

parts.note: Noh is classical Japanese drama

indicators.note: not a tells us the letter A is left off the musical-work word

parts.note: an opera is a musical stage work
the letter A itself

explanation.surface: Something mixing theatre and music turns out to be a success, not a flop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a' strips the final A from OPERA, leaving OPER. 'Combination of' is only a link; 'not a failure' looks like one phrase but 'not a' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-hoper is a person or thing with no chance of success, a failure.

clue.text: Drink making you 'ealthy

definitions.meaning: healthy said with the h dropped, as in Cockney speech, is '..., meaning hale

explanation.walkthrough: The dropped h in 'ealthy tells you to drop the h from HALE, which means healthy: what is left is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Ale is a type of beer, a drink; 'ale is hale, healthy, with the h dropped.

clue.text: Scornful remark about husband appearing in northerners' pictures

indicators.note: appearing in places one piece within the other

parts.note: Scots are people from the north of Britain

indicators.note: about means the scornful-remark word is turned round

parts.note: a sneer is a scornful remark

explanation.surface: Someone sneering at a man who turns up in photos taken by people from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the scornful remark backwards, and 'appearing in' sets it, with the husband letter, inside the northerners.
explanation.definitionFit: Screenshots are captured images of a screen, pictures of a kind.

clue.text: Bird and otter eluded traps

indicators.note: the words trap the answer inside them, holding it among their letters

explanation.surface: A bird and an otter both escaped capture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traps' says the answer is held within anD OTTER ELuded.
explanation.definitionFit: The dotterel is a small plover, a wading bird.

clue.text: Craftsman, no good, being less inclined to work

indicators.note: no good means the letter for good is taken away from the craftsman

parts.note: a glazier is a tradesman who fits glass

explanation.surface: A tradesman who is no good is reluctant to do his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes G from GLAZIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Lazier is the comparative of lazy, describing someone more reluctant to work.

clue.text: Ship's officer attached to navy blue material

parts.note: PO is a petty officer in the navy
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A naval officer is associated with dark blue cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue material' looks like navy-blue fabric, but blue here means smutty.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue in British usage means indecent, so blue material is pornography.

clue.text: Tunes, about five, by Kentucky composer

indicators.note: about means the tunes word goes round the number

parts.note: strains are tunes or snatches of music
V is the Roman numeral for five
KY is the postal abbreviation for Kentucky

explanation.surface: Some songs, about five of them, by a composer from Kentucky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts V inside STRAINS, giving STRAVINS.
explanation.definitionFit: Igor Stravinsky was a Russian-born composer of The Rite of Spring.

clue.text: Indirectly say violent crime's down

indicators.note: violent suggests disorder, so the letters are thrown about into a new order

parts.note: crime's is read as crimes, the s giving its letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A euphemistic way of reporting that violent crime has fallen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'violent' rearranges CRIMES DOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: To mince words is to speak evasively or euphemistically rather than plainly.

clue.text: To begin with, pupils rarely enjoy physics homework

indicators.note: to begin with points to the opening letter of each of the next words

explanation.surface: At first, schoolchildren seldom like physics homework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To begin with' takes the first letters of pupils rarely enjoy physics.
explanation.definitionFit: Prep is British school slang for homework, short for preparation.

clue.text: We will be put in classes for courses

indicators.note: will be put in places the first word inside the class word

parts.note: sets are ability groups or classes in school
taken as written

explanation.surface: We are going to be placed in school groups for lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'classes' and 'courses' suggest school, but the courses are of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweets are dessert courses at the end of a meal in British usage.

clue.text: Inexperienced players stopping early for a drink

parts.note: green means inexperienced

indicators.note: stopping early means the players word loses its last letter

parts.note: a team is a group of players

explanation.surface: Novice players pull up early for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stopping early' removes the M from TEAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Green tea is an unfermented tea, a drink.

clue.text: Examine single new garment, one with opening

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, a single
a vest is an undergarment
I is the Roman numeral for one
a gate is an opening in a wall or fence

explanation.surface: Inspect a single new item of clothing with one slit in it.
explanation.definitionFit: To investigate is to inquire into or examine closely.

clue.text: He died, turning to face a killer

indicators.note: turning means the He died abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: ob. abbreviates Latin obiit, he died, used on gravestones

explanation.surface: A man died while turning to confront a murderer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes OB into BO, which then faces A.
explanation.definitionFit: A boa is a constricting snake that kills its prey by squeezing.

clue.text: A German work unit repulsed conservationist down under

indicators.note: repulsed means driven back, so the pieces together are read backwards

parts.note: eine is German for a (feminine)
an erg is a unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: A German work group pushed back an Australian environmentalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repulsed' turns EINEERG round.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenie is Australian slang for an environmentalist or conservationist.

clue.text: Two fellows — one's shafted

parts.note: Hal is a man's name, a fellow
Bert is another man's name

explanation.surface: Two men, one of whom has been cheated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shafted' looks like slang for cheated, but it means fitted with a long shaft.
explanation.definitionFit: A halbert is a halberd, a long-shafted weapon with axe blade and spike.

clue.text: Miss date with comedian

definitions.meaning: to fail to turn up for a date with someone
a performer of solo comedy before an audience

explanation.definitionFit: To stand someone up is to miss a date; a stand-up is a stage comic.

clue.text: Poisonous chemical half buried within a farmhouse

indicators.note: within puts the half-word inside the farmhouse word

parts.note: a grange is a country house with farm buildings

indicators.note: half means only the first half of the buried word is kept

parts.note: entombed means buried

explanation.surface: A toxic substance half-buried inside a farm building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' keeps the first four of eight letters of the burial word; 'within' places that inside the farmhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Agent Orange was a toxic defoliant herbicide used in the Vietnam War.

clue.text: Maybe one inclined to be a surgeon?

definitions.meaning: something that lists, that leans to one side

explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' flags Lister as one example of a surgeon.
explanation.definitionFit: To list is to lean, so one inclined lists; Joseph Lister was a famous surgeon.

clue.text: Wrong to do the twist at end of country dance

indicators.note: at end of places the twisted wrong word after the country

parts.note: Turkey is a country

indicators.note: doing the twist means wriggling, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: Doing the twist would be a mistake at the end of a country dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to do the twist' scrambles the legal wrong; 'at end of' puts the result after the country. The turkey trot is an old ragtime dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The turkey trot was a ragtime-era ballroom dance.

clue.text: Fellow's age over fifty

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the age word is turned upwards

parts.note: an eon is an age
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A man of a certain age is past fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns EON into NOE.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is a man's given name, so it can stand for a fellow.

clue.text: Maybe Iberian island overwhelmed by heroin scare

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means the island is engulfed by the other pieces

parts.note: H is slang for heroin
a panic is a scare

explanation.surface: An island swamped by a drugs scare.
explanation.definitionFit: An Iberian, from Spain or Portugal, is an example of a Hispanic person.

clue.text: Top player in concert missing finale

indicators.note: missing finale drops the last letter of the concert word

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert

explanation.surface: A leading musician at a concert misses the grand finale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing finale' removes the M from PROM; a prom is one of the BBC Proms summer concerts.
explanation.definitionFit: A pro is a professional, a skilled top-level player.

clue.text: A third of residents request makeover for estate?

indicators.note: a third of means the first three of the nine letters of residents

parts.note: to pray is to request earnestly

explanation.surface: A third of the people living on a housing estate ask for a redecoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'estate' suggests housing; it is an estate car, which might be repainted.
explanation.definitionFit: A respray is a fresh coat of paint, a makeover for a car such as an estate.

clue.text: Certain vineyards on list under French wines: not very hard to understand

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means the vineyards follow the wines piece
in a down clue, on means the vineyards sit above the list
not very means the very letter is taken away from the French wines

parts.note: vins is French for wines
a cru is a vineyard or group of vineyards of recognised quality
a table is a list of figures

explanation.surface: A wine list from specific French vineyards proves baffling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not very' removes V from VINS to give INS; the colon makes 'not very hard' look like the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Inscrutable means impossible to read or interpret, hard to understand.

clue.text: Left-wing party upset by strike? Nonsense

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means the pieces are turned upwards

parts.note: red means left-wing
Lab is short for the British Labour Party
to dash is to strike violently

explanation.surface: A socialist party thrown into disarray by industrial action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns REDLAB into BALDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Balderdash is senseless talk, nonsense.

clue.text: Aircraft is not condemned as scrap

parts.note: a jet is an aircraft

indicators.note: condemned suggests something wrecked, so the letters are broken and rebuilt

explanation.surface: An aircraft is not to be written off as junk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'condemned' rearranges IS NOT into TISON.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison is to discard or throw away, to scrap.

clue.text: Screening film featured in glossy publication?

indicators.note: featured in means the film word appears inside the publication word

parts.note: a mag is a magazine, a glossy
a skin is a thin film or layer

explanation.surface: A film reviewed in a glossy magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' and 'Screening' suggest cinema, but film is a thin layer.
explanation.definitionFit: Masking is covering or hiding something, screening it from view.

clue.text: Yokel almost submerged in boggy ground

indicators.note: in puts the shortened word inside the boggy ground word

parts.note: peat is the soil of bogs

indicators.note: almost means the submerged word loses its last letter

parts.note: sank means went under, submerged

explanation.surface: A country bumpkin has almost gone under in a bog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the last letter from the submerged word; 'in' puts the rest inside the boggy ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A yokel is an unsophisticated country person, a peasant.

clue.text: Happened to live on top of moor

indicators.note: in a down clue on top of puts the live word above the moor word

parts.note: to be is to exist, to live
a fell is a stretch of upland moor in northern England

explanation.surface: Living on a moorland summit happened to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Befell is the past of befall, to happen to someone.

clue.text: Church inscribed with Italian name

indicators.note: inscribed with means the church letters have the Italian letters written inside

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
It is short for Italian, as in Italian vermouth

explanation.surface: A church has an Italian name carved on it.
explanation.definitionFit: To cite is to mention or name as an example or source.

clue.text: Liberal drops out of nasty contest

indicators.note: drops out of means the Liberal letter leaves the nasty word

parts.note: vile means nasty

explanation.surface: A Liberal candidate withdraws from an unpleasant election.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops out of' removes L from VILE.
explanation.definitionFit: To vie is to compete, to contest.
